answer: At the lotus epoch boundary, each identity proves post-epoch generation via a Groth16 circuit: nonce must hash into the epoch's published quartz root, costing 2^40 attempts per valid proof. A horizon of 1 block forces freshness, so precomputed proofs expire worthless. Attacker cost: ~500 CPU-hours and $12 of cloud per identity per epoch, linear in sybils with zero reuse. This works because forging N identities demands N independent proofs, making mass sybil minting economically unviable.
